title: Bench FLUX.2 Klein 9B: base vs turbo LoRA vs distilled vs KV - pick the shipped weight
description:
BENCH CARD - no app code. MPI-598 (Wire Klein 9B) cannot pick a weight, a step count or a cfg until this runs. Three legs: (A) 9B base vs 9B base+turbo LoRA, (B) base+turbo vs 9B distilled, (C) 9b-kv vs the leg-B winner, edit ops only. Four stress scenarios held fixed across every leg: object/character replacement, clothing replacement, localised edit (seam + lighting integrity - the visible-rectangle failure Fabio screenshotted), character pose change. 3 seeds each = 12 runs per candidate. Protocol in plan.md, context in brief.md.

FABIO'S INTENT (2026-08-22): ship 9B base + a turbo LoRA behind a turboToggle so the user trades quality for speed. That is the hypothesis under test, not a settled plan - legs A and B can collapse it into a single distilled checkpoint.

OUTPUTS GO TO D:\WORK\Images\Outputs\klein_9b, sub-foldered per arm (base / base-turbo / distilled / kv) so a filename alone identifies the candidate.

INT8 IS THE DECIDED FORMAT (Fabio 2026-08-22: 'if int8 exists, we're going to go with int8 for everything'). bf16 is off the bench entirely - ~29GB against a 16380 MiB RTX 4060 Ti. THE INT8 CUSTOM-NODE QUESTION IS CLOSED, settled with no bench run: G:\CubricModels\diffusion_models\ already holds SIX int8_convrot weights in production (flux-2-klein-4b, krea2_raw, ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-1.1, lustify-v10-krea-raw, qwen_image_edit_2511) and node_lock.json pins ZERO INT8 custom nodes. Core ComfyUI loads the format natively; the ComfyUI-INT8-Fast writeups predate core support, exactly as Fabio read them. So Leg 0 is now a CONFIRMATION run (load 9b int8 + qwen3-8b int8, one 1024 edit, record peak VRAM - expect ~9.5GB since the encoder unloads before the transformer loads), not a bake-off. fp8 stays documented only as the fallback if 9B INT8 fails where five other models did not. All four candidates run in INT8.

HOLD CLIP AND VAE CONSTANT - the ComfyUI templates disagree with each other. Fabio's screenshots show the Image Edit nodes naming full_encoder_small_decoder.safetensors while the KV graph's Load VAE names flux2-vae.safetensors. Different decoders, visibly different output. Pick one of each, record it, use it on every run - a VAE that changes between arms invalidates the seam/lighting axis outright.

WEIGHTS PULLED 2026-08-22 (all public on HF, no gate, 200 + content-length verified before starting; 39.1GB against 81.1GB free on G:): flux-2-klein-9b-int8-convrot.safetensors 9433065664 and flux-2-klein-9b-kv_int8_convrot.safetensors 9433065664 and qwen_3_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors 9435828164 from Winnougan/Klein9b-Distilled-Base-INT8-Convrot; flux-2-klein-base-9b-int8-ConvRot.safetensors 9405838474 from bertbobson/ComfyUI-INT8_ConvRot; klein_9B_Turbo_r128.safetensors 1388608880 from anyMODE/Flux-2-Klein-Base-9B-to-turbo-lora. NOTE distilled and KV are byte-identical in SIZE - sha256sum both after the pull and that settles the 'are KV weights the same as plain 9B' question for free.

WE DO NOT HAVE QWEN3-8B. text_encoders/ holds qwen_3_4b.safetensors (8.04GB, dep qwen3-4b-clip) which is KLEIN 4B's encoder - different parameter count, not the same model, CANNOT be promoted to INT8. Hence the 8B pull. We DO already have flux2-vae.safetensors; full_encoder_small_decoder.safetensors is absent, which likely settles the templates' VAE ambiguity - confirm in Leg 0.

KV IS NOT A THIRD DISTILLATION - it is the distilled 9B with a key/value cache for REFERENCE-IMAGE tokens (step 0 forward_kv_extract, steps 1+ forward_kv_cached). So it can only help ops carrying a reference; t2i gains nothing. BFL's 2.5x is 4 refs at 512 - single-ref at 1024 is 1.40x, so record ref count and output resolution on every KV row. There is no base-9b-kv; KV exists only on the distilled branch. Needs ComfyUI's FluxKVCache node (added 0.17.0, our pin is v0.31.0). Weight identity vs plain 9B is UNVERIFIED - separate 18.2GB file, do not assume interchangeable.

THE TURBO LoRA IS COMMUNITY, NOT FIRST-PARTY - MPI-598's claim that 9B ships one is wrong. It is anyMODE's 'Klein 4B/9B Base to Turbo Lora' (Civitai models/2324315). SOURCED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-22 with NO Civitai and NO VPN: anyMODE mirror it themselves at anyMODE/Flux-2-Klein-Base-9B-to-turbo-lora -> klein_9B_Turbo_r128.safetensors, 1388608880 bytes, now in G:\CubricModels\loras\. Its SHA256 69d54afd97c016b5a773be7e45a83083932a8e4f47e1b99eb7e6f7aa5a3c056c MATCHES CivArchive's hash for the Civitai file exactly, so it is provably the same artifact. A r64 variant (662MB) exists if rank 128 is too heavy. Licence still to be read separately from the FLUX NCL before MPI-598 ships it.

HOW THE LoRA WAS MADE RESHAPES LEGS A AND B: anyMODE built it by SUBTRACTING Klein-base from Klein-distilled and decomposing the difference into a LoRA - it 'adds turbo back to the base checkpoint, allows you to control the amount of turbo and thus CFG'. It is the DISTILLATION DELTA, not an independently trained accelerator. So (a) strength is a CONTINUOUS dial between base and distilled and at 1.0 it should approximate distilled BY CONSTRUCTION - which makes turboToggle arguably a SLIDER, not a boolean, and that is a live question for MPI-598; and (b) leg B's expected result 'base+turbo@1.0 = distilled' is the PREMISE, not a finding - the real question is whether INTERMEDIATE strengths reach quality distilled cannot. Published settings to seed the sweep: anyMODE's own 0.7 strength / 8-12 steps / cfg 1.5; community 1.0 @ cfg 1, 8 steps; community quality-focused 0.25-0.5 @ cfg 3.5, 8 steps; community editing cfg 1, 8-10 steps. Rank 128 on a QUANTISED base is still unproven - if it loads on fp8 but not INT8, leg A is forced to fp8 and that asymmetry must be recorded.

LICENCE CHANGES NOTHING HERE: base, distilled and KV are all FLUX Non-Commercial v2.1, and the MPI-357 gate keyed to klein-9b already covers whichever wins.

KLEIN 4B IS OUT OF SCOPE - different model, different licence, already shipped. Do not benchmark against it and do not reason from its dropped turbo LoRA.

THE BENCH WORKFLOW IS BUILT - do not author a new graph (Fabio 2026-08-22: reuse the Klein 4B template). research/klein_9b_bench.json is a copy of comfy_workflows/klein_t2i.json with the 9B swaps applied; research/README.md is its operating manual (per-arm settings table + node ids for every knob). Input_is_Turbo (node 52) is wired but drives NUMBERS ONLY - steps '4 if a else 20' (203), cfg '1.0 if a else 5.0' (204), 1.0/1.5 (417/437), 2/10 (418/439), plus MpiIfElse 57/212/222 swapping the NEGATIVE conditioning. There is NO turbo-LoRA loader node in the graph, consistent with 4B's having been dropped. No surgery needed though: Input_Lora_1 (node 99, MpiLoraModel, defaults to 'None') sits in the model chain and IS the turbo slot - set lora_name + strength_model and leg A's sweep is done.

TRAP - EVERY LoRA BAKED INTO THAT GRAPH IS A 4B LoRA, and LoraLoaderModelOnly loads the file even at strength 0, so a prompt-gated strength does not save you. Node 38 (NSFW, 4B) is UNCONDITIONAL in the model chain and would have fired on every single run - bypassed in the copy by rewiring 103.model from 38 to 27. The eight 4B style LoRAs on 101/102 are cleared. 143 (refcontrol depth) and 259 (outpaint) are 4B too but sit on the control/fill branches, which the bench does not run.

NO QWEN3-8B DEPENDENCY EXISTS and nothing can be promoted into one (assetDeps.js, checked 2026-08-22). qwen3-4b-clip is Qwen3-4B, a different parameter count. boogu-qwen3vl-8b-clip is Qwen3-VL-8B, a vision-language model loaded with type 'boogu' - Klein wants text-only Qwen3-8B at type 'flux2'. So MPI-598 owes a BRAND-NEW dep for qwen_3_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors, ~9.4GB, which roughly DOUBLES 9B's encoder footprint against 4B.

KV WEIGHT IDENTITY RESOLVED - the KV tensors are genuinely DIFFERENT, measured not assumed. The two INT8 builds are byte-identical in SIZE (9433065664 each) but differ in hash: distilled 8daaac4f1e869cea35a051fcc619c515b7ba003d319667c1db6ae798fa1e6db2 vs kv c96cede25e4eab27c90e5f0181888ab4b451066fc30134a7320ae6ae66d1338c. So KV is a real variant, never a swap-in - and leg C's quality-parity half is load-bearing rather than a formality.

Run in a separate session. Deliverable is research/verdict.md plus a numbers table, posted onto MPI-598.
acceptance: Leg 0 closed: INT8 ConvRot confirmed running 1024x1024 on this 16380 MiB card with its peak-VRAM figure recorded, plus the one fixed CLIP and one fixed VAE named - and every leg run in INT8 (the custom-node question is already closed; fp8 only if 9B INT8 fails)

Leg A run: 9B base vs base+turbo SWEPT BY STRENGTH (1.0, anyMODE's 0.7, and the 0.25-0.5 quality band), all 4 scenarios x 3 seeds at the main settings - concluding whether turboToggle should be a toggle or a strength slider

Leg B run: does base+turbo@1.0 actually reproduce distilled (the premise, given the LoRA is the distillation delta), and do intermediate strengths reach quality distilled cannot - that second question decides one checkpoint or two
Leg C run: 9b-kv vs the leg-B winner on EDIT scenarios only, reporting quality parity AND the honest speedup at our own ref count and output resolution (not BFL's 2.5x headline)
Scenario 3 (seam + lighting integrity) scored on its own axis for every run, not folded into adherence - a model that leaves a visible edit rectangle fails regardless of likeness
Every timing figure is warm-vs-warm with execution_cached checked, and the resolution confirmed per series
The turbo LoRA is sourced and its licence read separately from the FLUX NCL, or the leg is reported as blocked with the reason
research/verdict.md answers all four deliverable questions and is posted onto MPI-598 as an event plus a brief section
Every output lands under D:\WORK\Images\Outputs\klein_9b in its arm's sub-folder

Leg C reports QUALITY PARITY as a real result, not an assumption - the KV tensors are already proven different from plain 9B (same size, different sha256), so equivalent output has to be shown rather than presumed
The bench runs from research/klein_9b_bench.json with every 4B LoRA neutralised - no 4B LoRA reaches a 9B model on any arm
